title: Persistent spatial neighborhoods and changing stromal–vascular states accompany postnatal heart development
central_message: Postnatal cardiac development is consistent with regional remodeling of recurring multicellular neighborhoods: fibroblast matrix specialization, vascular growth and CM developmental programs change together, but do not follow a single synchronized maturation axis.
sections: Recurring anatomical organization anchors the developmental comparison
Regional CM identity overlaps with local vascular-response programs
Fibroblast state remodeling occurs within overlapping interstitial environments
Vascular growth and capillary apposition relate to different CM components
Transport compares remodeling neighborhoods but does not identify unique developmental fates
A regional tissue-unit model yields discriminating experiments
data_scope: Secondary analysis, one spatial section/age, no new biological replication
